mainTopic: Bowing in prayer, signs of accepted prayer, and the hidden rewards of the righteous
overview: The amud opens with rules for when a כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל and a king bow during the עמידה, then defines three kinds of bowing and reports how אביי ורבא bowed. The גמרא resolves conflicting ברייתות about bowing in מודים, defending רבא's practice by limiting the disapproval to the הודאה of הלל and of ברכת המזון. A new משנה teaches that a mistake in תפילה is a bad sign, while רבי חנינא בן דוסא knew his prayer was accepted when it flowed smoothly. The גמרא says the key ברכה is אבות and gives a פסוק as the source for רבי חנינא's sign. Teachings of רבי יוחנן about rewards that 'no eye has seen' lead to disputes with שמואל about ימות המשיח and with רבי אבהו about בעלי תשובה. Stories of רבי חנינא בן דוסא healing through prayer follow, along with rules about praying in a room with windows. The פרק ends with the הדרן for פרק אין עומדין.

steps.title: Where a high priest and a king bow
steps.stepSummary: The passage gives different bowing points for a כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל and a king.
steps.simpleTranslation: A כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל bows at the end of every blessing. A king bows at both the beginning and the end of every blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: The passage continues a rule about bowing during prayer. It names where a כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל and a king bow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The king bows at more points than the כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל in this version. This is the rule that the next report will present differently.

phrases.aramaic: כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל, בְּסוֹף כׇּל בְּרָכָה וּבְרָכָה.
phrases.english: A high priest: at the end of each and every blessing.
And the king: at the beginning of each and every blessing
and at the end of each and every blessing.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל, בְּסוֹף כׇּל בְּרָכָה וּבְרָכָה.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This passage begins in the middle of an existing discussion.

steps.title: A different report of the bowing rules
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר נחמני reports a different explanation from רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: An ordinary person follows the rule already stated. A כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל bows at the beginning of every blessing. Once a king bows, he does not straighten up again; the account of שלמה's prayer is cited as support.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק בר נחמני gives a different version of the rules, which he says he heard explained by רבי יהושע בן לוי. He then cites a פסוק about שלמה to support the rule for a king.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל now bows at the beginning, rather than the end, of each blessing. The king's rule also changes: instead of bowing at repeated points, he remains bowed once he has bowed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzḥak bar Naḥmani said:

phrases.aramaic: לְדִידִי מִפָּרְשָׁא לִי מִינֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: It was explained to me by Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi himself:
An ordinary person, as we said.

phrases.aramaic: כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל, תְּחִלַּת כׇּל בְּרָכָה וּבְרָכָה.
phrases.english: A high priest: at the beginning of each and every blessing.

phrases.aramaic: הַמֶּלֶךְ — כֵּיוָן שֶׁכָּרַע שׁוּב אֵינוֹ זוֹקֵף,
phrases.english: The king: once he has bowed, he does not straighten up again,
as it is stated: “And when Solomon finished praying, etc.,”

phrases.aramaic: קָם מִלִּפְנֵי מִזְבַּח ה׳ מִכְּרֹעַ עַל בִּרְכָּיו״.
phrases.english: “he rose from before the altar of the Lord, from kneeling upon his knees.”

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר נַחְמָנִי: לְדִידִי מִפָּרְשָׁא לִי מִינֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This report gives different bowing rules for the כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל and the king.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל bows at the beginning of each blessing; once a king bows, he does not straighten up again.

steps.title: The meaning of bowing on the face
steps.stepSummary: A teaching defines קִידָּה and gives a verse as its example.
steps.simpleTranslation: קִידָּה means bowing on one's face, as the פסוק says that בת שבע bowed with her face toward the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The discussion moves from rules about when to bow to the meanings of words for bowing. The first definition is קִידָּה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching pairs the word קִידָּה with a verse that mentions the person's face. It is defining a form of bowing, not adding another point in prayer when someone must bow.

phrases.english: The Sages taught: Kidda means bowing on one's face,
as it is stated: “Bathsheba bowed with her face to the ground.”

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: קִידָּה — עַל אַפַּיִם,
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After mentioning the king's bow, the passage begins defining different forms of bowing.

steps.title: The meaning of kneeling
steps.stepSummary: The teaching defines כְּרִיעָה using the פסוק about שלמה's knees.
steps.simpleTranslation: כְּרִיעָה means kneeling on the knees, as the verse says, “from kneeling upon his knees.”
steps.whatsHappening: The teaching gives its second definition: כְּרִיעָה is a bow on the knees. It supports that meaning with words from the פסוק about שלמה just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the body part named in the verse is the knees. That distinguishes כְּרִיעָה from the face-down קִידָּה described immediately before it.

phrases.english: Keria means bowing on one's knees,
as it is stated: “from kneeling upon his knees.”

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּרִיעָה — עַל בִּרְכַּיִם,
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is the second definition in the same teaching.

steps.title: The meaning of full prostration
steps.stepSummary: The teaching defines הִשְׁתַּחֲוָאָה as spreading out the hands and feet.
steps.simpleTranslation: הִשְׁתַּחֲוָאָה is stretching out the hands and feet. The teaching cites the question, “Shall I, your mother, and your brothers come to bow down to you to the ground?”
steps.whatsHappening: The teaching gives its third definition, הִשְׁתַּחֲוָאָה, and cites a verse about bowing to the ground. This completes its list of three forms of bowing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This form is described by the position of both the hands and the feet. The three definitions help the learner keep the passage's different bowing words separate.

keyTerms.meaning: stretching out the hands and feet

phrases.english: Hishtaḥava'a means stretching out the hands and feet,
as it is stated: “Shall I, your mother, and your brothers come
to bow down to you to the ground?”

steps.triggerLanguage: הִשְׁתַּחֲוָאָה — זוֹ פִּשּׁוּט יָדַיִם וְרַגְלַיִם,
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This completes the teaching's three definitions.
steps.whatToRemember: The teaching distinguishes קִידָּה on the face, כְּרִיעָה on the knees, and הִשְׁתַּחֲוָאָה with hands and feet stretched out.

steps.title: An observed way of bowing
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בריה דרב הונא describes how he saw אַבָּיֵי and רָבָא bow.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא בריה דרב הונא said: I saw אַבָּיֵי and רָבָא bowing by tilting to the side.
steps.whatsHappening: The passage stays on the subject of bowing and turns to an observation. רב חייא בריה דרב הונא reports how אַבָּיֵי and רָבָא bowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier teaching defined forms of bowing, including full הִשְׁתַּחֲוָאָה with hands and feet stretched out. This report shows that אַבָּיֵי and רָבָא did not do the full form. They only tilted to the side.

keyTerms.meaning: tilting to the side (not full prostration)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Ḥiyya, son of Rav Huna, said:
I saw Abaye and Rava
leaning to the side (not fully prostrating).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא:
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defining three forms of bowing, the passage reports an observed way of bowing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב חייא בריה דרב הונא saw אַבָּיֵי and רָבָא bow by tilting to the side.

steps.title: Two teachings disagree about bowing in the thanksgiving blessing
steps.stepSummary: One ברייתא says bowing in הודאה is praiseworthy, and another says it is reprehensible.
steps.simpleTranslation: One ברייתא teaches: someone who bows in the הודאה blessing is praiseworthy. Another ברייתא teaches: he is reprehensible!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets two ברייתות side by side that seem to say opposite things about bowing in מודים. This is a contradiction that needs to be solved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both ברייתות describe the exact same action: bowing in הודאה. One calls it משובח (praiseworthy) and the other calls it מגונה (reprehensible). The גמרא now has to find a difference between the two cases.

keyTerms.meaning: Thanksgiving; here, the מודים blessing of שמונה עשרה

phrases.english: One baraita taught:
One who bows in the thanksgiving blessing —
this is praiseworthy.
And another baraita taught:
this is reprehensible!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי חֲדָא וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After describing the types of bowing, the גמרא turns to a contradiction about bowing in הודאה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The halachic status of bowing in the הודאה blessing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two ברייתות give opposite rulings on the identical act.

steps.title: Beginning of the blessing versus the end
steps.stepSummary: The praise refers to bowing at the beginning of הודאה, and the condemnation refers to bowing at the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this ברייתא speaks about bowing at the beginning, and that ברייתא speaks about bowing at the end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא solves the contradiction by explaining that each ברייתא is talking about a different moment in the blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bowing at the start of מודים is praiseworthy. Bowing at the end is called מגונה. Each ruling now has its own case, so the two ברייתות no longer clash.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the opening of a resolution
This one ... that one; splits two sources into two cases

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this means bowing in הודאה is bad in general. The answer only separates timing: bowing at the beginning is praised, and only bowing at the end is discouraged.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one refers to the beginning,
that one refers to the end.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בַּתְּחִלָּה, הָא לְבַסּוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case distinction (הא בהא): two different points in the blessing
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seemed to be about the identical bow.
steps.terutzMaskana: Bowing at the beginning of הודאה is משובח, and bowing at the end is מגונה.

steps.title: רבא bowed at both the beginning and the end
steps.stepSummary: רבא's practice was to bow in הודאה at both the beginning and the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא bowed in the הודאה blessing at the beginning and at the end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports what רבא actually did. This sets up the next steps, because his practice seems to go against the conclusion just reached.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said bowing at the end is מגונה. Yet רבא bowed at the end too. This report creates tension that the next steps will explore.

phrases.english: Rava bowed in the thanksgiving blessing
at the beginning and at the end.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא כָּרַע בְּהוֹדָאָה תְּחִלָּה וָסוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents a practice that seems to conflict with the distinction drawn in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא bowed in הודאה at both the beginning and the end.

steps.title: The רבנן ask רבא why he does this
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן ask רבא for the reason behind his practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן said to him: Why does the master act this way?
steps.whatsHappening: The students ask רבא to explain why he bows at the end, since that seems to be discouraged. This sets up his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is respectful, using the title מר, but it carries a real challenge. It asks for his source for an unusual practice.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis; here, scholars or students around רבא
Master; a respectful way to address a sage

phrases.english: The Rabbis said to him:
Why does the master do this?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַבָּנַן: אַמַּאי קָא עָבֵיד מָר הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the practice described in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source or reason for רבא bowing at the end of הודאה.

steps.title: רבא relies on what he saw his teachers do
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that he saw רב נחמן and רב ששת bow this way.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I saw רב נחמן bow, and I saw רב ששת do the same.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains that his practice comes from watching two great teachers, רב נחמן and רב ששת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not give a logical argument. He relies on the actual behavior of earlier sages, which is a strong source in the גמרא. The next steps test how this practice fits with the ברייתא that calls bowing in הודאה מגונה.

phrases.english: He said to them:
I saw Rav Naḥman, who bowed,
and I saw Rav Sheshet
who did so as well.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְהוּ: חֲזֵינָא לְרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבא based his practice on watching רב נחמן and רב ששת bow at both the beginning and the end.

steps.title: Challenge to רבא from the teaching that calls it reprehensible
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא's practice from the ברייתא that says bowing in הודאה is מגונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא: one who bows in הודאה is reprehensible?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא (and the teachers he followed) from the ברייתא quoted earlier. רבא's answer comes in step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to step 8, that ברייתא refers to bowing at the end. Since רבא bowed at the end too, he seems to be doing exactly what the ברייתא calls מגונה. The גמרא will need a new way to read that ברייתא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge forces the גמרא to look again at what the 'reprehensible' ברייתא really means. It shapes the final practice for bowing in מודים.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: one who bows in thanksgiving —
this is reprehensible!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא הַכּוֹרֵעַ בַּהוֹדָאָה הֲרֵי זֶה מְגוּנֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the practice that רבא defended in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's practice of bowing at the end of הודאה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Step 8 applied the 'reprehensible' ברייתא to bowing at the end, which is exactly what רבא did.

steps.title: The disapproving ברייתא is about the הודאה in הלל
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the ברייתא calling bowing in הודאה מגונה refers to the הודאה of הלל, not the הודאה of the עמידה.
steps.simpleTranslation: That ברייתא is talking about the thanksgiving that is in הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his practice. He says the ברייתא that disapproves of bowing is not about the עמידה at all. It is about the thanksgiving part of הלל ("הודו לה׳").
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge in step 12 assumed that 'הודאה' means the ברכה of מודים in the עמידה. רבא reads the word differently: it means the 'הודו' verses in הלל. Bowing there is wrong, but bowing in the עמידה's מודים is still fine.

keyTerms.meaning: That one (refers back to the ברייתא just quoted)
Thanksgiving. Here it could mean מודים in the עמידה or the 'הודו' verses
Psalms of praise recited on holidays, which include 'הודו לה׳ כי טוב'

phrases.english: That [baraita refers] to the thanksgiving that is in Hallel.
phrases.notes: Said by רבא in answer to the challenge in step 12.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהִיא בְּהוֹדָאָה שֶׁבְּ״הַלֵּל״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 12 by narrowing what the ברייתא means.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the source: the ambiguous word 'הודאה' is limited to the הודאה of הלל.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's 'הודאה' means מודים in the עמידה, so רבא's bowing would be מגונה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא refers to the 'הודו' of הלל, so bowing at מודים in the עמידה is allowed.

steps.title: A ברייתא that lists הלל separately
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן bring a ברייתא that mentions both 'הודאה' and 'הודאה של הלל' as separate items, so plain 'הודאה' cannot mean הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: One who bows in the thanksgiving, or in the thanksgiving of הלל, is acting disgracefully.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge comes back. A different ברייתא names the הודאה of הלל as its own item, so the plain word 'הודאה' must mean something else, apparently מודים in the עמידה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This attacks רבא's answer from step 13. If 'הודאה' already meant הלל, the ברייתא would not need to add 'and the הודאה of הלל'. So plain 'הודאה' must be the עמידה's מודים, and bowing there is called מגונה. That contradicts רבא's practice again.

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: One who bows in the thanksgiving
and in the thanksgiving of Hallel
phrases.notes: Since הלל is listed separately, the first 'הודאה' must mean something else.

phrases.english: this is disgraceful.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reading that the disapproving 'הודאה' is the הודאה of הלל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא lists 'הודאה' and 'הודאה של הלל' as two items. So plain 'הודאה' is not הלל and must be the עמידה, where bowing is called מגונה.

steps.title: That ברייתא is about the הודאה in ברכת המזון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the plain 'הודאה' in this ברייתא is the second ברכה of ברכת המזון ('נודה לך'), not the עמידה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When that ברייתא was taught, it was about the thanksgiving of ברכת המזון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא agrees that plain 'הודאה' here is not הלל. It identifies it as a third kind of thanksgiving: the ברכה of 'נודה לך' in ברכת המזון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists two places where you should not bow: ברכת המזון's הודאה and הלל's הודאה. The עמידה's מודים is not on that list, so רבא's bowing there stands. This ends the challenges to רבא's practice.

keyTerms.meaning: Grace after Meals. Its second ברכה begins 'נודה לך'

steps.whatToRemember: Bowing at מודים in the עמידה is proper (רבא bowed at its beginning and end). It is disgraceful to bow at the הודאה of הלל or at the הודאה of ברכת המזון.

phrases.english: When that [baraita] was taught,
it was about the thanksgiving of Grace after Meals.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי תַּנְיָא הַהִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 14 by moving the plain 'הודאה' to ברכת המזון.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the source: the unspecified 'הודאה' means a different prayer (ברכת המזון).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since הלל is listed separately, plain 'הודאה' must be the עמידה's מודים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Plain 'הודאה' is ברכת המזון's 'נודה לך'. The עמידה is untouched, and רבא's practice is upheld.

steps.title: A mistake in prayer is a bad sign
steps.stepSummary: New משנה: if a person makes a mistake in תפילה, it is a bad sign for him. If the שליח ציבור makes the mistake, it is a bad sign for the congregation, because a person's agent is like himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who prays and makes a mistake, it is a bad sign for him. And if he is the שליח ציבור, it is a bad sign for those who sent him, because a person's agent is like himself.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic. It teaches that making a mistake while praying signals that the prayer may not have been accepted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה applies this sign to a whole congregation when their שליח ציבור errs. Its reason is the general rule of agency, שלוחו של אדם כמותו: the leader acts on the congregation's behalf, so his stumble reflects on them.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. Marks the start of a new משנה
Prayer leader who prays on behalf of the congregation
A person's agent is considered like the person himself

steps.confusionAlert: Don't confuse the two rules here. The 'bad sign' is not a punishment and does not make the תפילה invalid. It is only a sign. The agency rule is brought only to explain why the congregation is affected.
steps.whyThisMatters: This uses a basic legal rule of agency (שליחות) to explain why the congregation shares in the sign when their leader errs.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who prays and makes a mistake
it is a bad sign for him.
And if he is the communal prayer leader
it is a bad sign for those who sent him,
because a person's agent is like himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַמִּתְפַּלֵּל וְטָעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with a new topic after the bowing discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mistake in תפילה is a bad sign for the one praying. If the שליח ציבור errs, it is a bad sign for the congregation, based on שלוחו של אדם כמותו.

steps.title: רבי חנינא בן דוסא predicts who will live
steps.stepSummary: The משנה tells that רבי חנינא בן דוסא would pray for the sick and then announce which one would live and which would die.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said about רבי חנינא בן דוסא that he would pray for the sick and say: This one will live, and this one will die.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a story that connects to the idea of signs in prayer. This line sets up the question and answer that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story builds on the rule in step 16. A mistake is a bad sign, and here a great צדיק used how his own prayer went to know the outcome. How he knew is explained in the next two steps.

keyTerms.meaning: They said about him. Introduces a story about a sage

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן דּוֹסָא
phrases.english: They said about Rabbi Ḥanina ben Dosa
that he would pray for the sick,
and say: 'This one will live, and this one will die.'

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: ראיה (the story illustrates the משנה's rule about signs in prayer)
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן דּוֹסָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the משנה's idea that how a prayer goes is a sign.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חנינא בן דוסא, after praying for the sick, could tell who would live and who would die.

steps.title: How did he know?
steps.stepSummary: People ask רבי חנינא בן דוסא how he knew who would live and who would die.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: How do you know?
steps.whatsHappening: People ask רבי חנינא בן דוסא how he could know the outcome. This sets up his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a sincere request for information, not a challenge. They are not doubting him. They want to know what sign he relied on.

keyTerms.meaning: From where, or how (do you know)?

phrases.english: They said to him: From where do you know?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: מִנַּיִן אַתָּה יוֹדֵעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the knowledge described in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How רבי חנינא בן דוסא knew whether a sick person would live or die.

steps.title: Smooth prayer means it was accepted
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בן דוסא explains: if his prayer flowed smoothly, he knew it was accepted. If not, he knew it was rejected.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: If my prayer flows smoothly in my mouth, I know that it is accepted. And if not, I know that it is rejected.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא בן דוסא answers. The sign was how his prayer came out: smoothly, or with stumbling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the positive side of the משנה's rule. A mistake is a bad sign, so a fluent prayer is a good sign. רבי חנינא בן דוסא read his own fluency as a sign of whether Heaven accepted the request.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה teaches that how a prayer flows is a sign. A mistake is a bad sign, both for an individual and for a congregation through its שליח ציבור. A smooth, fluent prayer, as רבי חנינא בן דוסא described, is a sign that the prayer was accepted.

phrases.english: He said to them:
If my prayer flows fluently in my mouth
I know that it is accepted.
And if not
I know that it is rejected.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם: אִם שְׁגוּרָה תְּפִלָּתִי בְּפִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A fluent prayer is a sign it was accepted. A halting prayer is a sign it was rejected.

steps.title: Which blessing does the משנה mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which ברכה the משנה is talking about when it says a mistake in תפילה is a bad sign.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: On which ברכה does this apply?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the משנה. It asks: the משנה said a mistake in תפילה is a bad sign, but a mistake in which ברכה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא understands that the משנה is not talking about a slip anywhere in the עמידה. So there must be one specific ברכה where a mistake counts as a סימן רע. The גמרא asks which one it is.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion section that explains the משנה
'On which one?', asking which specific item is meant
A bad sign or bad omen

phrases.english: Gemara: On which one?
phrases.notes: Refers back to the משנה's statement that a mistake in prayer is a bad sign (step 16).

steps.triggerLanguage: אַהֵיָיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story of רבי חנינא בן דוסא and returns to the first statement of the משנה (step 16) to explain it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which ברכה of the עמידה is meant, where a mistake is a bad sign?

steps.title: The answer: ברכת אבות
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא, quoting רב ספרא in the name of a scholar from רבי's academy, says the משנה refers to ברכת אבות, the first ברכה of the עמידה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא said in the name of רב ספרא, who said it in the name of one of the scholars of רבי's academy: In 'אבות.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. A mistake is a bad sign only when it happens in the first ברכה, ברכת אבות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ברכת אבות is the opening ברכה of the עמידה, the moment a person first stands before הקב״ה. If his תפילה stumbles right at that start, it is taken as a sign that his prayer is not being accepted. Mistakes in later ברכות do not carry this meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: The first ברכה of the עמידה, which mentions the Patriarchs (מָגֵן אַבְרָהָם)
'In the name of', a chain of quotation
One of the scholars of the academy of רבי (רבי יהודה הנשיא)

phrases.english: Rav Chiyya said
phrases.notes: He's the first person in the chain passing this teaching along.

phrases.english: Rav Safra said
phrases.notes: Second link in the chain.

phrases.english: in the name of one of the scholars of Rebbi's academy:
In 'Avos' (the blessing of the Patriarchs).
phrases.notes: This is the actual answer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא אָמַר רַב סָפְרָא מִשּׁוּם חַד דְּבֵי רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The bad sign applies to a mistake in ברכת אבות.

steps.title: A second version attaches the statement to a ברייתא about כוונה
steps.stepSummary: Some teach the same statement on a different source: a ברייתא saying a person should have כוונה in all the ברכות, and if he cannot, then at least in one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach this statement on a ברייתא instead: One who prays must focus his heart in all the ברכות. If he cannot focus in all of them, he should focus his heart in one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of where רב ספרא's statement was originally said. This step quotes the ברייתא and sets up the next step, where the same answer, 'אבות,' will be applied to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version the statement 'באבות' was never about the משנה's bad sign. It explains the ברייתא's word 'one,' meaning the one ברכה where כוונה is a must. The ברייתא gives an ideal (כוונה in every ברכה) and a minimum (at least one ברכה).

keyTerms.meaning: 'Some teach it', which introduces a different version of the tradition
A teaching of the תנאים not included in the משנה
To focus one's heart, meaning to have כוונה (concentration) in prayer
In all of them, meaning all the ברכות of the עמידה

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument against step 21. It is the same statement by the same people, only remembered as attached to a different source. The words are identical, but the topic changes from a mistake being a bad sign to where כוונה is required.

phrases.english: Some teach it on a baraita:
phrases.notes: This brings a different version of how the teaching was passed down.

phrases.aramaic: הַמִּתְפַּלֵּל צָרִיךְ שֶׁיְּכַוֵּין אֶת לִבּוֹ בְּכוּלָּן,
phrases.english: One who prays must focus his heart in all of them,
phrases.notes: The ideal: כוונה in every ברכה.

phrases.english: and if he is unable to focus in all of them,
he should focus his heart in one.
phrases.notes: The minimum. Which 'one' is meant is explained in the next step.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּמַתְנֵי לַהּ אַבָּרַיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternate version of where the statement in step 21 was said.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ideally a person has כוונה in all the ברכות of the עמידה. At the very least, he must have כוונה in one.

steps.title: In the second version, 'one' means ברכת אבות
steps.stepSummary: On this ברייתא, רבי חייא, quoting רב ספרא in the name of a scholar from רבי's academy, explains that the 'one' ברכה requiring כוונה is ברכת אבות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא said in the name of רב ספרא, who said it in the name of one of the scholars of רבי's academy: In 'אבות.'
steps.whatsHappening: The same chain of scholars says the same word, 'באבות,' but here it explains the ברייתא. The minimum ברכה where a person must have כוונה is ברכת אבות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said 'one' without naming it. This statement fills the gap: if a person can only focus in one ברכה, it must be the first one, ברכת אבות. The opening of the עמידה is the most important place for כוונה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'In one', the single ברכה that is the minimum for כוונה

steps.whatToRemember: Both versions point to ברכת אבות as the key ברכה of the עמידה. In the first version, a mistake there is a bad sign. In the second version, it is the one ברכה where כוונה is required at minimum.
steps.whyThisMatters: The second version is the basis for the practical rule that כוונה in ברכת אבות is essential to the עמידה, even though a person ideally tries to focus throughout.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya said
phrases.notes: Notice that here it says רבי, not רב.

phrases.english: Rav Safra said
in the name of one of the scholars of Rebbi's academy:
In 'Avos.'
phrases.notes: Here this defines the 'one' ברכה from the ברייתא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא אָמַר רַב סָפְרָא מִשּׁוּם חַד דְּבֵי רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the open word 'באחת' in the ברייתא quoted in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The minimum ברכה requiring כוונה is ברכת אבות.

steps.title: Where do we learn that smooth prayer is a good sign?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about רבי חנינא בן דוסא and asks for the source of this idea.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said about רבי חנינא בן דוסא that he could tell whether his prayer was accepted. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the line in the משנה about רבי חנינא בן דוסא. It asks where we learn that smooth, fluent prayer shows the prayer was accepted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה reported רבי חנינא בן דוסא's method but gave no source for it. The גמרא wants to know what basis there is for treating smooth speech in prayer as a sign that Heaven accepted it.

keyTerms.meaning: They said about him (a phrase that introduces a report about a person)
Etc. (shows that only the beginning of the quote is given)
From where are these words derived? (a request for a source)

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבִּי חֲנִינָא וְכוּ׳:
phrases.english: They said about Rabbi Chanina, etc.:
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה about רבי חנינא בן דוסא

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the רבי חנינא בן דוסא line of the משנה, which was explained in Step 19, and asks for its scriptural source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that fluent prayer is a sign the prayer was accepted.

steps.title: The source is a פסוק in ישעיה about the 'fruit of the lips'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי brings a פסוק linking speech of the lips with healing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: The פסוק says, 'He creates the expression of the lips: Peace, peace, to the far and to the near, says ה׳, and I will heal him.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי answers the question with a פסוק from ישעיה. When ה׳ grants a person smooth speech, healing follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק first mentions ה׳ creating the 'expression of the lips' and ends with 'I will heal him.' This shows that when the words come out easily, the request, such as praying for a sick person, will be granted.

keyTerms.meaning: Expression or speech of the lips

steps.whatToRemember: Fluent prayer is a sign of acceptance, based on the פסוק 'בורא ניב שפתים... ורפאתיו'.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
As the verse states:
"He creates the expression of the lips,
phrases.notes: ישעיה נ״ז:י״ט

phrases.english: Peace, peace, to the far and to the near,
says the Lord, and I will heal him."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source made in Step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ישעיה נ״ז:י״ט: when ה׳ creates smooth speech of the lips, healing follows.

steps.title: The reward of those who support תלמידי חכמים, and of the scholars themselves
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that the נביאים described the reward of people who support תלמידי חכמים, but the scholars' own reward is beyond what any eye has seen.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: All the נביאים prophesied only about someone who marries his daughter to a תלמיד חכם, does business for a תלמיד חכם, or benefits a תלמיד חכם with his property. But for the תלמידי חכמים themselves, 'No eye has seen, God, except You, what He will do for those who wait for Him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רבי יוחנן to close the topic. The good things the נביאים promised were for people who support Torah scholars, while the reward of the scholars themselves is too great to describe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נביאים' descriptions of future good have a limit, and they cover the supporters of תלמידי חכמים. The scholars' own reward goes beyond prophecy. The proof is the פסוק saying that only God has seen it.

keyTerms.meaning: One who marries off his daughter
No eye has seen (the reward is beyond description)

steps.confusionAlert: This does not say that supporters get a small reward. It says their reward is great but can still be described by prophecy, while the scholars' own reward cannot be described at all.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
All the prophets, all of them, prophesied only
about one who marries his daughter to a Torah scholar,
and one who does business for a Torah scholar,
and one who benefits a Torah scholar from his property.
But Torah scholars themselves —
"No eye has seen it, God, except You,
phrases.notes: ישעיה ס״ד:ג׳

phrases.english: what He will do for those who wait for Him."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כׇּל הַנְּבִיאִים כּוּלָּן לֹא נִתְנַבְּאוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new אגדה teaching that closes the section on prayer. It is not connected to Step 25 by argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The נביאים described the reward of those who support תלמידי חכמים. The reward of the תלמידי חכמים themselves is beyond prophecy.

steps.title: The נביאים described ימות המשיח, but not עולם הבא
steps.stepSummary: A second teaching of רבי יוחנן: prophecy covers ימות המשיח, while עולם הבא is beyond what any eye has seen.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: All the נביאים prophesied only about ימות המשיח. But about עולם הבא, 'No eye has seen, God, except You.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching of רבי יוחנן built the same way as the first. The wonders the נביאים described are about ימות המשיח, while עולם הבא is beyond description.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This teaching uses the same pattern and the same פסוק as Step 26, but applies it to time periods instead of people. It implies that ימות המשיח will be a time of great change in the world, the kind the נביאים described. That point sets up the next step.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
All the prophets, all of them, prophesied only
about the days of the Messiah,
but about the World to Come,
"No eye has seen it, God, except You."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel teaching from the same speaker, with the same pattern and the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The prophecies of good describe ימות המשיח. עולם הבא is beyond all prophecy.

steps.title: שמואל disagrees: ימות המשיח differs only in freedom from foreign rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבי יוחנן's view disagrees with שמואל. שמואל says the only difference between our world and ימות המשיח is that the Jews will no longer be ruled by other nations.
steps.simpleTranslation: This disagrees with שמואל, because שמואל said: The only difference between this world and ימות המשיח is that we will no longer serve foreign kingdoms. As it says, 'For the poor will never stop existing in the land.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבי יוחנן's last teaching argues with שמואל's view. It then quotes שמואל and his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said the נביאים' great promises are about ימות המשיח, so that era will be a time of great change. שמואל holds that ימות המשיח will be like our world except for political freedom. His proof is the פסוק saying poor people will always exist, which means the natural order stays the same. On שמואל's view, the נביאים' great promises must therefore refer to עולם הבא.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces a פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן holds that ימות המשיח will be a time of great change, described by the נביאים. שמואל holds that the only change in ימות המשיח will be freedom from שעבוד מלכויות.
steps.confusionAlert: 'ופליגא' is not an attack that needs an answer. The גמרא is simply noting that two אמוראים disagree.

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Shmuel,
for Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין בֵּין הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לִימוֹת הַמָּשִׁיחַ
phrases.english: There is no difference between this world and the days of the Messiah
except servitude to foreign kingdoms alone.
As it is stated:
"For the poor shall not cease from the land."
phrases.notes: דברים ט״ו:י״א

steps.triggerLanguage: וּפְלִיגָא דִּשְׁמוּאֵל, דְּאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רבי יוחנן's view in Step 27 disagrees with שמואל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to שמואל, ימות המשיח differs from this world only in freedom from שעבוד מלכויות. The natural order, including the existence of poverty, stays the same.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: There are two views of ימות המשיח: רבי יוחנן sees a transformed world, while שמואל sees only national freedom.

steps.title: Prophecies were about בעלי תשובה, but צדיקים גמורים get a hidden reward
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא quotes רבי יוחנן: the נביאים only described the reward of בעלי תשובה. The reward of צדיקים גמורים is beyond what any eye has seen.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חייא בר אבא said that רבי יוחנן said: All the prophets only prophesied about people who did תשובה. But about the completely righteous, the פסוק says: 'No eye has seen it, God, except for You.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third teaching of רבי יוחנן built on the same pattern: the נביאים describe one group's reward, but another group's reward is hidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 26 and 27 used this pattern for supporters of תלמידי חכמים and for ימות המשיח. Now רבי יוחנן applies it to two kinds of people. בעלי תשובה get a reward the prophets could describe, while צדיקים גמורים get a reward no eye has seen. So in רבי יוחנן's view, the צדיק גמור is on the higher level.

keyTerms.meaning: People who sinned and then repented
Completely righteous people who never fell into sin
'No eye has seen it', a phrase for a hidden reward beyond description

steps.confusionAlert: This is a different teaching from step 26, even though it uses the same פסוק and the same pattern. Here the contrast is between בעלי תשובה and צדיקים גמורים, not between supporters of scholars and the scholars themselves.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said
Rabbi Yochanan said:
All of the prophets, every one of them, did not prophesy
phrases.notes: These are the prophecies of comfort and reward.

phrases.english: except about penitents,
but about the completely righteous,
'No eye has seen it, God, except for You.'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו סד:ג

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third teaching of רבי יוחנן in the same 'prophets versus no eye has seen' pattern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The prophecies of reward were said about בעלי תשובה. The reward of צדיקים גמורים is hidden and beyond description, so they stand higher.

steps.title: רבי אבהו disagrees: בעלי תשובה stand higher than צדיקים גמורים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רבי יוחנן disagrees with רבי אבהו. רבי אבהו holds that בעלי תשובה reach a place that צדיקים גמורים cannot, and proves it from the order of a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this disagrees with רבי אבהו, because רבי אבהו said: In the place where בעלי תשובה stand, even צדיקים גמורים do not stand. As the פסוק says: 'Peace, peace, to the one who is far and to the one who is near.' It says 'to the one who is far' first, and only afterwards 'to the one who is near.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that a different אמורא, רבי אבהו, holds the opposite view of רבי יוחנן, and it quotes his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן ranked צדיקים גמורים higher. רבי אבהו ranks בעלי תשובה higher. His proof is that the פסוק greets 'the far one' first, and he understands 'far' as the sinner who came back. This sets up a challenge to רבי יוחנן, since the פסוק seems to support רבי אבהו.

keyTerms.meaning: And it disagrees with (the גמרא noting a dispute between opinions)
To the one who is far
To the one who is near

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the famous source for the idea that 'where בעלי תשובה stand, even צדיקים גמורים cannot stand,' a well-known principle about the power of תשובה.

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rabbi Abbahu,
as Rabbi Abbahu said:
The place where penitents stand,
the completely righteous do not stand there,
as it says: 'Peace, peace, to the far one and to the near one.'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו נז:יט

phrases.english: 'To the far one' comes first, and only then 'to the near one.'
phrases.notes: רבי אבהו reads 'far' as the sinner who has returned, so he is greeted first.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּפְלִיגָא דְּרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents an opposing view to רבי יוחנן's teaching in step 29, backed by a פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בעלי תשובה stand on a higher level than צדיקים גמורים, as shown by the פסוק greeting 'the far one' first.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן reads 'far' and 'near' the other way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains how רבי יוחנן would answer: 'far' means the צדיק who was always far from sin, and 'near' means the בעל תשובה who was once close to sin and only now moved away.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן would tell you: What does 'far' mean? Someone who was far from sin from the very start. And what does 'near' mean? Someone who was close to sin and has now moved away from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן by showing that רבי אבהו's פסוק can be read in a way that fits רבי יוחנן's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that 'the far one' is greeted first. They argue over who 'the far one' is. רבי אבהו says it is the בעל תשובה, but רבי יוחנן says it is the צדיק who was always distant from sin, so the פסוק actually puts the צדיק first. This removes רבי אבהו's proof without proving רבי אבהו wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Would say to you (a way of showing how one side would answer)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up who is 'far' and who is 'near.' רבי אבהו says 'far' is the בעל תשובה. רבי יוחנן says 'far' is the צדיק, far from sin, and 'near' is the בעל תשובה, who used to be near sin.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן and רבי אבהו disagree about who is greater, the צדיק גמור or the בעל תשובה. The dispute comes down to how each one reads 'far' and 'near' in the פסוק.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan would say to you:
What is meant by 'far'?
One who was far from sin from the very start.
phrases.notes: This is the צדיק גמור.

phrases.english: And what is meant by 'near'?
One who was close to sin,
and has now distanced himself from it.
phrases.notes: This is the בעל תשובה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר לְךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Neutralizes רבי אבהו's proof from the פסוק by reinterpreting it in line with רבי יוחנן.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the פסוק, not רבי אבהו's position itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי אבהו assumed 'far' means the בעל תשובה, but it can just as easily mean the one who was always far from sin.

steps.title: What is the hidden reward of 'no eye has seen'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the phrase 'עין לא ראתה' and asks what reward it actually refers to.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reward called 'no eye has seen'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what specific reward is hidden behind the phrase used in רבי יוחנן's teachings. This question sets up the two answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן used 'עין לא ראתה' several times to describe a reward beyond description. Now the גמרא wants to know what that reward concretely is.

phrases.english: What is 'No eye has seen it'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״עַיִן לֹא רָאָתָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי יוחנן and רבי אבהו dispute and returns to the phrase 'עין לא ראתה' from רבי יוחנן's teachings.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The concrete identity of the hidden reward described as 'עין לא ראתה'.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי: wine preserved since creation
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי says the hidden reward is wine that has been kept inside its grapes since the six days of creation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: This is the wine that has been kept in its grapes since the six days of creation.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי gives the first answer to what 'עין לא ראתה' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine still sealed inside the grape has never been seen by anyone. That fits the words 'no eye has seen it' exactly. It is a reward prepared from the very beginning of the world and kept hidden until now.

keyTerms.meaning: The preserved wine, kept hidden for the future

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
This is the wine that is preserved in its grapes
since the six days of creation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The hidden reward is wine kept inside its grapes since creation, which no eye has seen.

steps.title: רבי שמואל בר נחמני: it is עדן
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני gives a second answer: the hidden reward is עדן, a place no creature's eye has ever looked upon.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said: This is עדן, which the eye of no creature has ever looked upon.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא offers a different answer to the same question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי pointed to something hidden inside something else, wine inside grapes. רבי שמואל בר נחמני points to a place, עדן, which no living being has ever seen. Both answers explain 'no eye has seen' literally, as something that has truly never been viewed.

keyTerms.meaning: Eden, a hidden place of reward

steps.confusionAlert: עדן here is not the same as גן עדן where אדם lived. Steps 35–38 distinguish between the גן (the garden) and עדן itself, which no eye has seen.
steps.whatToRemember: Two views of 'עין לא ראתה': רבי יהושע בן לוי says preserved wine, and רבי שמואל בר נחמני says עדן.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said:
This is Eden,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא שָׁלְטָה בּוֹ עֵין כׇּל בְּרִיָּה.
phrases.english: which the eye of no creature has ever gazed upon.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second, different answer to the question of step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The hidden reward is עדן, which no creature has ever seen.

steps.title: But didn't אדם הראשון see עדן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that no eye has ever seen עדן: surely אדם הראשון was there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps you will say: where was אדם הראשון? (Wasn't he in עדן and didn't he see it?)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem with רבי שמואל בר נחמני's claim that no creature ever saw עדן. Didn't אדם הראשון live there?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 34 said עדן is a place no eye has ever seen. But the תורה tells us אדם הראשון lived in גן עדן. So it seems at least one person did see it.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps you will say (introduces a possible objection)

phrases.english: Perhaps you will say:
Where was Adam the first man?
phrases.notes: Meaning: wasn't he in Eden, so didn't he see it?

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁמָּא תֹּאמַר: אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן הֵיכָן הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי שמואל בר נחמני's claim in step 34
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that no eye has ever seen עדן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אדם הראשון lived in גן עדן, so he must have seen עדן

steps.title: אדם הראשון was only in the גן
steps.stepSummary: The answer: אדם הראשון was in the גן, not in עדן itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the גן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers in one word: אדם הראשון was in the גן, the Garden, not in עדן itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer separates two places. The Garden is where אדם הראשון lived. עדן is a different, higher place that he never saw. So the claim from step 34 still holds.

phrases.english: In the Garden.
phrases.notes: He was in the Garden, not in Eden itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 35
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Adam lived in Eden, so he saw it
steps.terutzMaskana: Adam lived only in the Garden, which is not Eden itself

steps.title: Maybe the גן and עדן are the same place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: perhaps גן and עדן are just two names for one place.
steps.simpleTranslation: And perhaps you will say: the Garden is Eden. They are one and the same.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer. Maybe 'גן' and 'עדן' are just two names for the same place, so אדם הראשון did see עדן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 36 only works if the Garden and Eden are truly different places. This challenge suggests they might be the same, which would bring back the original problem.

keyTerms.meaning: It is the same as (identifying two things)

phrases.english: And perhaps you will say:
The Garden is the same as Eden,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשֶׁמָּא תֹּאמַר: הוּא גַּן, הוּא עֵדֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the distinction made in step 36
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that Adam was only in the Garden and not in Eden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If Garden and Eden are one place, being in the Garden means being in Eden

steps.title: A פסוק proves the גן and עדן are separate
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says a river goes out from עדן to water the גן, so they are two separate places.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse teaches: 'And a river went out from Eden to water the Garden.' So the Garden is one place and Eden is another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק to prove that the Garden and Eden are two different places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A river flows out of עדן and goes to water the גן. Something that flows from one place to another shows there are two places. This confirms that אדם הראשון, who lived in the גן, never saw עדן.

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches (introduces a proof from a פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמואל בר נחמני, the hidden reward is עדן, which no one has ever seen, not even אדם הראשון, who lived only in the separate גן.

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
"And a river went out from Eden
phrases.notes: בראשית ב:י

phrases.english: to water the Garden,"
The Garden is separate and Eden is separate.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 37 with a proof from a פסוק
steps.raayaObject: That Garden and Eden are two separate places
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית ב:י, 'A river goes out from עדן to water the גן'

steps.title: רבן גמליאל's son falls ill and רבי חנינא prays
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells how רבן גמליאל sent two scholars to ask רבי חנינא בן דוסא to pray for his sick son, and he went up to his attic and prayed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Once רבן גמליאל's son became sick. He sent two תלמידי חכמים to רבי חנינא בן דוסא to pray for him. When רבי חנינא saw them, he went up to the attic and prayed for the boy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story about the power of רבי חנינא בן דוסא's prayer. It returns to the משנה's account of how he knew whether his prayer was accepted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא בן דוסא was mentioned in the משנה as someone whose prayers were answered. Now the גמרא tells stories to show this. Even a great leader like רבן גמליאל turned to him to pray.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁחָלָה בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל.
phrases.english: There was an incident where Rabban Gamliel's son became sick.
He sent two Torah scholars
to Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa
to pray for mercy for him.
As soon as he saw them,
he went up to the attic,
and prayed for mercy for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁחָלָה בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: stories about רבי חנינא בן דוסא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חנינא בן דוסא was asked to pray for רבן גמליאל's son and did so

steps.title: רבי חנינא announces the fever has left
steps.stepSummary: Coming down, רבי חנינא tells the messengers to go, because the fever has left the boy.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he came down he said to them: Go, the fever has left him.
steps.whatsHappening: After praying, רבי חנינא בן דוסא tells the messengers that the boy is already healed. This sets up their surprised question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He speaks with full confidence even though the boy is far away. That confidence is what the messengers will question next.

phrases.english: When he came down, he said to them:
Go, for the fever has left him.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּירִידָתוֹ אָמַר לָהֶם: לְכוּ, שֶׁחֲלָצַתּוּ חַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חנינא declares the boy healed

steps.title: Are you a prophet?
steps.stepSummary: The messengers ask how he could know this. Is he a prophet?
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Are you a prophet?!
steps.whatsHappening: The messengers are amazed and ask how he can know the boy is healed. Is he a נביא?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing what is happening far away seems to need נבואה. Their question pushes רבי חנינא to explain where his knowledge comes from.

phrases.english: They said to him: Are you a prophet?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: וְכִי נָבִיא אַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions his claim in step 40
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How he knows the boy is healed

steps.title: A fluent prayer is an accepted prayer
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא says he is not a prophet. He has a tradition: if his prayer flows smoothly, it was accepted, and if not, it was rejected.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I am not a prophet or the son of a prophet. But I have a tradition: if my prayer flows smoothly in my mouth, I know it is accepted. If not, I know it is rejected.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא explains that he is not a נביא. He has a sign from tradition: when his תפילה flows easily, he knows it was accepted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His knowledge does not come from נבואה. It comes from a received sign about how his own prayer went. A smooth prayer means it was accepted, and a stumbling prayer means it was rejected.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי חנינא is not claiming to be a נביא. His sign is about how his own prayer went, not about seeing the future.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sign is the reason the גמרא brings the story. It ties into the משנה's teaching that a fluent prayer is a good sign.

phrases.english: He said to them:
I am not a prophet
nor am I the son of a prophet,
phrases.notes: Wording from עמוס ז:יד

phrases.english: but this is the tradition I received:
If my prayer flows smoothly in my mouth,
I know that it is accepted,
and if not,
I know that it is rejected.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נָבִיא אָנֹכִי וְלֹא בֶן נָבִיא אָנֹכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 41
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He knows from the sign of a smoothly flowing prayer, not from prophecy

steps.title: The exact moment is confirmed
steps.stepSummary: The scholars wrote down the time. רבן גמליאל swore that at exactly that moment the fever broke and his son asked for water.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sat, wrote down, and noted the exact moment. When they came to רבן גמליאל, he said: I swear by the Temple service, you were not early or late. At exactly that moment the fever left him and he asked us for water.
steps.whatsHappening: The story's ending proves רבי חנינא was right. The boy was healed at the exact moment he said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scholars recorded the time so they could check it later. רבן גמליאל confirms it with an oath, so there is no doubt the תפילה worked right away.

keyTerms.meaning: By the Temple service (a form of oath)
You were not early and not late

phrases.english: They sat and wrote
and noted that exact moment.
When they came to Rabban Gamliel,
he said to them: I swear by the Temple service,
you were not early and you were not late,
rather, this is how it happened:
at that very moment the fever left him
and he asked us for water to drink.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָשְׁבוּ וְכָתְבוּ וְכִוְּונוּ אוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms that the sign in step 42 was accurate
steps.raayaObject: That רבי חנינא's prayer was accepted at the moment he said
steps.raayaSupportSource: The written time compared with רבן גמליאל's sworn testimony

steps.title: רבי חנינא heals רבי יוחנן בן זכאי's son
steps.stepSummary: In a second story, רבי יוחנן בן זכאי asks his student רבי חנינא to pray for his sick son. He puts his head between his knees, prays, and the boy lives.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another incident: רבי חנינא בן דוסא went to learn תורה from רבי יוחנן בן זכאי, and רבי יוחנן בן זכאי's son became sick. He said: חנינא my son, pray for him so he will live. He put his head between his knees and prayed, and the boy lived.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a second story about the power of רבי חנינא בן דוסא's prayer, this time for his own teacher's son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here even his own רבי, a very great sage, asks the student to pray. Putting his head between his knees shows deep, focused prayer, and it works.

phrases.aramaic: וְשׁוּב מַעֲשֶׂה בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן דּוֹסָא
phrases.english: And another incident with Rabbi Chanina ben Dosa,
who went to learn Torah
from Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai,

phrases.aramaic: וְחָלָה בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai's son became sick.
He said to him: Chanina, my son,
pray for mercy for him so that he will live.
He put his head between his knees
and prayed for mercy for him, and he lived.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשׁוּב מַעֲשֶׂה בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן דּוֹסָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story on the same theme
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חנינא's prayer heals רבי יוחנן בן זכאי's son

steps.title: רבי יוחנן בן זכאי says his own prayer would not work
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן זכאי says that even if he prayed with his head between his knees all day, Heaven would not pay attention to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן זכאי said: If בן זכאי had pressed his head between his knees the whole day, they would not have paid attention to him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן בן זכאי admits that his own prayer would not have worked like his student's did. This sets up his wife's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is surprising, because he is the teacher and the greater scholar. That surprise leads to the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: If only, had it been that

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Zakkai said:
Had ben Zakkai pressed
his head between his knees
the entire day,
they would not have paid attention to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי: אִלְמָלֵי הֵטִיחַ בֶּן זַכַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יוחנן בן זכאי reacts to the success of step 44
steps.mimraCoreRuling: His own prayer would not have been answered like רבי חנינא's

steps.title: His wife asks: is חנינא greater than you?
steps.stepSummary: His wife asks whether רבי חנינא is greater than him.
steps.simpleTranslation: His wife said to him: Is חנינא greater than you?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן בן זכאי's wife asks the obvious question: if חנינא's prayer works better, is he greater than you?
steps.deeperAnalysis: She assumes a better-answered prayer means a greater person. The answer in the next step will show that this is not the reason.

phrases.english: His wife said to him:
Is Chanina greater than you?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרָה לוֹ אִשְׁתּוֹ: וְכִי חֲנִינָא גָּדוֹל מִמְּךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about what he said in step 45
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי חנינא's greater success in prayer means he is greater

steps.title: A servant before the King versus a minister
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן זכאי answers no: רבי חנינא is like a servant before the King, and he is like a minister before the King.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to her: No. But he is like a servant before the King, and I am like a minister before the King.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן בן זכאי explains that רבי חנינא is not greater. They simply have different kinds of closeness to the King, הקב״ה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A servant is always in the King's house and can ask for small things at any time. A minister is more important, but he comes only when called and for big matters. So רבי חנינא's prayers get answered more often, even though he is not greater.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי חנינא בן דוסא's prayers were answered because of his constant, servant-like closeness to הקב״ה, not because he was greater than רבי יוחנן בן זכאי.
steps.confusionAlert: The minister is the more important position. The servant has more easy, everyday access. Do not read this as saying רבי חנינא was the greater person.

phrases.english: He said to her: No,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא הוּא דּוֹמֶה כְּעֶבֶד לִפְנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ,
phrases.english: but he is like a servant before the King,
and I am like a minister before the King.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הוּא דּוֹמֶה כְּעֶבֶד לִפְנֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wife's question in step 46
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not greater. A servant has constant access to the King, while a minister comes only for major matters.

steps.title: Pray only in a room with windows
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא quotes רבי יוחנן: a person should pray only in a house that has windows. The source is the פסוק about דניאל praying by open windows facing ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: A person should only pray in a house that has windows. As it says: 'He had open windows in his upper room, facing ירושלים.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about where to pray. A room with windows is the proper place, and a פסוק about דניאל is the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ואמר' (and he said) ties this teaching to the earlier statements about תפילה. The windows help a person look toward the sky and toward ירושלים and focus his heart. The proof is that דניאל, a great צדיק, chose to pray at open windows.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said, which introduces a פסוק as a source

steps.whyThisMatters: This teaching is brought down להלכה. The שולחן ערוך rules that one should ideally pray in a room with windows, preferably facing ירושלים.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said
Rabbi Yochanan said:
phrases.notes: רבי חייא בר אבא is passing on his teacher's statement.

phrases.english: A person should not pray
except in a house that has windows there.
As it is said:
"And he had open windows in his upper room
facing Jerusalem."
phrases.notes: Some versions have לָקֳבֵל (in round brackets); the corrected wording is נֶגֶד (in square brackets). Both mean 'facing.' The פסוק is דניאל ו:יא.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the story of רבי חנינא בן דוסא's תפילה to a new practical rule about the place of תפילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One should pray only in a room with windows, as דניאל did.

steps.title: Praying in an open field is brazen
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא says he considers a person brazen if he prays in an open field.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: I consider brazen someone who prays in an open field (a valley).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another rule about where to pray. רב כהנא calls a person who prays out in an open field brazen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said what the right place for תפילה is. רב כהנא now names a wrong place. In a closed, private space a person feels humble before the King, while praying out in the open looks careless and lacks that humble awe. The מפרשים also note that out in the open he is easily distracted by people passing by.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse this with יצחק praying in the field (לָשׂוּחַ בַּשָּׂדֶה). The מפרשים explain that רב כהנא means a field where people pass by. A secluded spot is different.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
I consider brazen
one who prays in an open field.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: חֲצִיף עֲלַי מַאן דִּמְצַלֵּי בְּבַקְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the topic of the proper place for תפילה, now stating a place to avoid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Praying in an open field shows brazenness.

steps.title: Publicly spelling out one's sins is brazen
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא also says it is brazen to spell out one's sins. The proof is the פסוק 'אשרי נשוי פשע כסוי חטאה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב כהנא said: I consider brazen someone who spells out his sins. As it says: 'Happy is the one whose wrongdoing is forgiven, whose sin is covered.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second teaching from רב כהנא that uses the same wording, 'חציף עלי.' This time the subject is announcing one's sins, and a פסוק from תהלים is the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This teaching is placed here because it uses the same phrase as the last one. It is not on the same topic. The פסוק praises a person whose sin is 'covered.' Keeping one's sins private shows shame, and that shame brings forgiveness. Openly broadcasting them shows a lack of shame.

keyTerms.meaning: Who spells out or details his sin

steps.confusionAlert: This does not cancel וידוי. The גמרא in יומא (פו:) explains that this refers to sins between a person and ה׳. Those should not be announced publicly. Sins against other people must be confessed openly.

phrases.english: And Rav Kahana said:
I consider brazen one who spells out his sin,
as it is said:
"Happy is he whose transgression is forgiven,
whose sin is covered over."
phrases.notes: תהלים לב:א

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: חֲצִיף עֲלַי מַאן דִּמְפָרֵשׁ חִטְאֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brought because it shares רב כהנא's phrase 'חציף עלי.' The link is the matching wording, and it moves to a different topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One should not publicly spell out his sins, because covering them shows shame and brings forgiveness.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק אין עומדין
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for the fifth פרק of ברכות, פרק אין עומדין.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק אין עומדין.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the פרק. It is not part of the discussion. It is a goodbye to the פרק we just finished learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פרק began by saying one may stand to pray only with seriousness (כובד ראש). It ends with teachings on the humble, focused way to pray. The הדרן expresses the hope to come back and learn it again.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One may not stand,' the name of the fifth perek of ברכות

steps.whatToRemember: פרק אין עומדין is all about the right mindset for תפילה. Pray seriously and humbly, in a proper place like a room with windows, and keep private sins private.

phrases.english: We will return to you, "One may not stand"

steps.triggerLanguage: הדרן עלך אין עומדין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the perek after the last teaching of רב כהנא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The perek is complete. Its theme is serious, humble, focused תפילה.
